subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Normative Social Influence
description: A short lesson to help you apply Normative Social Influence.

hook.text: A teenager hates cigarettes but smokes because her friend group does. She conforms to belong, not because she agrees.

buildup.text: Normative influence is conforming to be accepted by the group, even when you privately disagree with the behavior.

discovery.text: Deutsch and Gerard separated two motives: we conform to be right and we conform to be liked. The second is stronger.

twist.text: Anonymous settings reduce normative influence. When nobody watches, people follow their true preferences more often.

climax.text: When you feel pressure to agree, ask: am I convinced or just afraid of rejection? The answer changes the decision.

punchline.text: Agreeing to belong is not the same as agreeing.

quiz.question: What is normative social influence?
options: Conforming because you believe the group is correct
Conforming to be accepted by the group despite private disagreement
